entries.name: forward-rule-call-removed
entries.claim: A1: the one call in #post is the only thing that refuses a family other than receipts and shipments an effective tenant business day after the recorded one. Deleting it admits an adjustment dated seven days ahead inside the seven-day scope, so the refusal the backdate test now declares never happens -- node reports the missing rejection, because assert.rejects skips its validator when nothing is thrown.

kills.name: the configured backdate window decides which effective period a posting may carry
kills.expected: Missing expected rejection: seven days ahead must be refused by the forward rule

entries.name: forward-rule-one-day-slack
entries.claim: A2: the rule has zero days of slack. Letting the effective day run one day past the recorded day admits a transfer dated 09:00 on the next Calgary business day, so the first refusal of the forward-rule test goes missing. Every other case in that test keeps its verdict under this mutation, which is what makes the red the slack's alone.

kills.name: the forward rule refuses the next tenant business day, counted in the tenant calendar and not in UTC
kills.expected: Missing expected rejection: the next tenant business day must be refused

entries.name: forward-rule-utc-days
entries.claim: A3: 'today' is the tenant's declared business day, not the UTC date. Handing the rule the UTC dates of the two instants instead of the tenant business periods refuses a posting at 19:00 Calgary time recorded at 17:00 the same evening -- 5 August in UTC, 4 August in Calgary -- by the forward rule's own code with the UTC dates in its message. The refusal and admission cases before it keep their verdicts, because there both calendars agree.

kills.name: the forward rule refuses the next tenant business day, counted in the tenant calendar and not in UTC
kills.expected: INVENTORY_FORWARD_DATE_REFUSED: effective period 2026-08-05 is after the recorded business day 2026-08-04
